sections.h2: Where is the Delta County, Michigan register of deeds?
sections.html:
The Delta County Register of Deeds is in the county building at 310 Ludington Street in Escanaba, the county seat. Office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., the phone is (906) 789-5100, and the fax is (906) 789-5179.

Delta County sits in the Upper Peninsula along the Lake Michigan shore. Its cities are Escanaba and Gladstone, its one village is Garden, and Rapid River and Rock are census-designated places. Whichever of those your house is in, the deed is recorded in Escanaba.

The county's own register page is short, so call before you drive in if you have an unusual instrument. Bring the original signed deed and payment for the recording fee, and ask whether the office can take a card.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Delta County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed costs $30 per document, because that is the flat amount in MCL 600.2567, which applies unless a charter county adopts a schedule of its own.

Statewide register of deeds charges that apply in Delta County
ServiceFee under MCL 600.2567
Record a document, any length$30.00
Assign or discharge several instruments in one paper$3.00 per additional instrument
Copies of records$1.00 per page
Certify a recorded document$5.00
Record search on request50 cents per year searched, $5 minimum
Filing another paper$1.00

The fee is due when the document is left for recording. Electronic filings paid electronically get one business day under the statute. Ask the office whether it takes e-recording and which vendors it works with.

sections.h2: How is Michigan transfer tax figured on a Delta County sale?
sections.html:
The seller owes the state tax of $3.75 and the county tax of $0.55 for each $500 of value or fraction of it. The county rate comes from MCL 207.504, and the state act at MCL 207.523 makes the seller liable and sends payment to the county treasurer where the land lies.

Consider a $150,000 sale, a bit under the Census Bureau's $157,100 median for Delta County owner-occupied homes. That is 300 units of $500, which gives $1,125 in state tax plus $165 in county tax, or $1,290 together.

  • Payment is due to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered to the buyer.
  • A deed must state its total value, or an affidavit declaring the value must be attached.
  • The state act exempts transfers under $100, security instruments, land contracts that do not pass title until paid, and conveyances to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • If a seller believes a sale qualified for an exemption after the tax was paid, MCL 207.523 lets the seller or the buyer who paid on the seller's behalf ask the Department of Treasury for a refund.

The county act has its own, shorter exemption list in MCL 207.505, so a family transfer can be exempt at the state level and still carry the county share. Ask the register how it will treat yours.

sections.h2: Does Delta County require a tax certificate before recording?
sections.html:
It does for most sale deeds. MCL 211.135 directs the register of deeds not to record a deed, plat or land contract until the county treasurer certifies liens and tax titles and confirms that taxes were paid for the five preceding years.

A quitclaim deed or other conveyance with no covenants of warranty is excepted. So are sheriff's deeds and certain tax deeds made by the state treasurer. The Delta County Treasurer's office handles the certification, collects delinquent property taxes, certifies deeds, and conducts the annual tax sale on behalf of the State Treasury, according to the county's treasurer page.

Ask the treasurer what the certificate fee is and how long it takes before you set a closing date. If the parcel carries delinquent taxes, get a payoff amount in writing so it can be paid from the seller's proceeds.

sections.h2: What should a Delta County seller know about assessment records?
sections.html:
Delta County's Equalization office sells the assessment records many buyers and title agents ask for. Its price list, effective April 10, 2026, includes a $5 Equalization Report, a $15 Apportionment Report showing millage rates, and $15 for taxable value by school district or township.

Other items include database copies at $1 per page, simple maps at $2 each, and a digital copy of the current assessment roll at $2,000. The office lists the name and address of property owners and the current assessed and equalized value of a property among the records it keeps.

For a single house, the local city or township assessor is the person to ask about the assessed and taxable value. Millage rates and the date a parcel's taxable value changes after a sale are the questions that matter most when a buyer is estimating the first year's tax bill.

sections.h2: What does the Delta County housing picture look like?
sections.html:
Delta County's median owner-occupied home value is $157,100 on the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates, well below Clinton County's. Median household income is $57,809, median gross rent is $692, and 82.0% of occupied homes are owner-occupied.

The county covers 1,991 square miles, but 820 of them are water, which leaves 1,171 square miles of land. It is the fifth-largest Michigan county by land area. Population was 36,903 in 2020 and is estimated at 36,582 for July 2025, a drop of 0.9%. About 28.2% of residents are 65 or older, and 12.1% live in poverty.

US 2 crosses the south of the county and US 41 runs north to south through its middle and along the Lake Michigan shore. Part of the Hiawatha National Forest lies inside the county. Delta County Airport, southwest of Escanaba, has scheduled airline service to Detroit and Minneapolis. Recreation and forest products are major industries, and health care and social assistance receipts were about $234 million in 2022.

sections.h2: How should I prepare a Delta County deed for recording?
sections.html:
Michigan's recording statute, MCL 565.201, sets one format for every county, and the Delta County register applies it.

  • Use original signatures with printed names, and keep the names consistent across the body, signature and acknowledgment.
  • List the full addresses of all parties and the name and address of the person who drafted the deed.
  • Have a notary, judge or court clerk acknowledge a deed signed in Michigan.
  • Leave the top 2.5 inches of the first page blank for recording stamps.
  • Do not include more than the last four digits of a Social Security number.

The county does not draft deeds or give legal advice. A title company or attorney can prepare the paper, and a seller who is clearing an inherited house should ask whether a death certificate or court order has to be recorded first.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Delta County, Michigan?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document, set by MCL 600.2567. An assignment or discharge of several instruments adds $3 for each extra one, and certifying a recorded document costs $5.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when a Delta County house is sold?
faqs.a: The seller pays. The rates are $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county on each $500 of value or fraction of it, due to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: Where do I send a deed for a house in Gladstone or Garden?
faqs.a: To the Delta County Register of Deeds in Escanaba at 310 Ludington Street. The register records deeds for the whole county, including both cities and the village.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate for a Delta County quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: No, a quitclaim deed with no covenants of warranty is excepted under MCL 211.135. A warranty deed or land contract needs the county treasurer's certificate before the register will record it.

faqs.q: When is the Delta County register of deeds open?
faqs.a: The office lists hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The county phone is (906) 789-5100. Call ahead on holidays or if you plan to bring a complicated document.
